text_01: This thesis built a complete real-time system for detecting and tracking moving objects in public environments on a Xilinx Zynq-7000 SoC: running on a ZYBO development board, whose SoC pairs an ARM processor with FPGA fabric, making it a natural target for HW/SW co-design. The design targeted high speed, high accuracy and strong security at once, while staying cost-effective and able to run standalone: no host PC in the loop.
text_02: The pipeline takes live video in over HDMI, isolates a target by color-range filtering, tracks it, and estimates the distance to the object from its apparent size. Results are shown simultaneously on an LED-matrix panel and a VGA monitor, while the distance telemetry streams out over UART.
text_03: The development flow moved from algorithm to silicon in three stages: the algorithms were first verified in MATLAB, then optimized in OpenCV, and finally synthesized to hardware with Vivado HLS, with the ARM software side built in the Xilinx SDK:  C, C++, HLS and Python across the stack.
